author: GamingBolt
description:
Games really should be faster to make, shouldn’t they? After all, engines have grown in power, middleware is more abundant, and hardware architecture now semi-ubiquitous. So what gives? 

Okay, gross over-simplication aside, here’s the bottom line: stronger tools have enabled loftier ambition, and that ambition has spiralled. Longer development cycles and skyrocketing budgets means the reality is fewer releases per studio. 

What’s more, expectation has grown in tandem with studio ambition. Publishers want bigger worlds, deeper mechanics, and sharper fidelity to match improvements in game development infrastructure, while players want value for money.
title: Why Are Games Taking FOREVER TO MAKE?

author: GamingBolt
description:
Outward 2 is poised to double down on everything that made the original so distinct – harsh survival systems, involved progression, and a refusal to hold your hand. 

With deeper mechanics, smoother combat, and a more dynamic world, it’s shaping up to be a far more demanding, and rewarding, adventure when it releases to early access on July 9th. Here’s fifteen things you need to know before you step foot in its wilds.
title: Outward 2 Early Access  - 15 Things You Need To Know Before You Buy

author: GamingBolt
description:
The live-service space has always felt a little make or break for those publishers daring enough to try and brave its many variables. But things have been changing over the years due to the failures of a few valid attempts at crafting experiences that are designed to have their players spending all, or most, of their limited gaming time in a specific world, engaging constantly with a specific gameplay loop.

It’s an approach that has its merits, but it's also one that comes with risks that a single-player title simply does not have to contend with. Well, we’re here to take a look at how modern gaming has seemingly come full circle, and give you a bit of insight into why that’s the case. Join us as we take a look at a rather intriguing pivot back to a formula that has worked once, and continues to hold its own against an equally compelling addition to modern gaming.
title: Gaming Is Running Back To Single-Player - Because The Live-Service Dream Collapsed
